audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagrees with both the packet chart and the already-audited mirror (aatrox__yone). Content had win[0]=Skill, win[1]=Yone, win[2]=Yone, win[3]=Skill, win[4]=Skill, win[5]=Yone; the mirror states Levels 1 through First item all read Aatrox and only Two+ items reads Yone.
audit.why: Aatrox's page already ships the Aatrox-favoured rows; mirror-fix.js would overwrite any disagreement, and the full/content layers must state the same row.
audit.corrected: win[0..5] and phases[0..5].side = Aatrox; win[6]/phases[6].side stay Yone. whys and phase whys rewritten so the reasons match the sides.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and late both claim the matchup flips on your first item, which contradicts the corrected chart and ignores that Umbral Dash healing is what actually holds the lane.
audit.why: Umbral Dash (E) is on 9/8/7/6/5s with passive healing on every champion hit, and World Ender increases that healing — a raw first item does not beat it. Grievous Wounds is the real spike.
audit.corrected: The flip is Executioner's Calling plus two items, not first item alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions Infernal Chains (W). It carries the grounding flag, and grounding denies Mortal Steel's two-stack dash and Fate Sealed's blink — the decisive interaction of this matchup.
audit.why: Yone's entire pattern is dash-in / snap-back; being grounded inside the chain zone removes both halves of it. Also missing: Deathbringer Stance is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up is the tell, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: Added Infernal Chains grounding (20/18/16/14/12s) to tldr, mid and breakdown.cooldowns; added the anti-heal requirement to the World Ender don't.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gave no numbers and repeated 'sweetspots knock up' — only the third cast's centre knocks up.
audit.why: The Darkin Blade is 14/12/10/8/6s; Infernal Chains 20/18/16/14/12s.

edits.before: By level 3 dodging his center Q makes trades even — skill decides.
edits.after: By level 3 his Q chain and Umbral Dash healing still edge trades.

edits.before: First item tips your DPS and kiting ahead of his Q cooldowns.
edits.after: First item still loses to his Q3 knockup and Umbral Dash healing.

edits.before: Q stacking and passive crits win the short trades. Identify how Aatrox contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: His Q out-ranges Mortal Steel at level 1, so take the safe last-hits and learn where he places the first sweetspot.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Aatrox must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but Umbral Dash (9s at rank 1) out-sustains your chip. Keep the wave near your side and take only the trades he starts.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on The Darkin Blade's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King helps, but anti-heal comes first — fight only when The Darkin Blade is down.

edits.before: Dodge his Q sweetspots — Q3-W trade, E to reset safe. Yone wins by trading around Aatrox's The Darkin Blade and cashing the pattern: win extended trades and E-reset.
edits.after: Dodge the Q3 centre and never fight inside Infernal Chains — it grounds you, so your Q3 dash and Fate Sealed will not fire. Trade when The Darkin Blade (14s at rank 1) is down.

edits.before: - Aatrox The Darkin Blade: matchup-defining — Sweetspots knock up. Dodge them. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Infernal Chains: 20s at rank 1 — its centre grounds you, denying your Q3 dash and Fate Sealed, so leave the zone before you commit. - The Darkin Blade: 14s at rank 1, and only the third cast's centre knocks up. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Sweetspots knock up. Dodge them. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Only the third cast's centre knocks up; at rank 1 it is down 14s — go then.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: World Ender raises his healing — land Executioner's Calling, then fight.

edits.before: Once you finish first item (usually Kraken/IE path) and can weave Q-airborne + E to reposition, the matchup flips. Bait his Q chain, E away through the knockups, then punish the long Q cooldown window.
edits.after: First item does not flip it yet — Umbral Dash, down to 5s at rank 5, keeps healing him through your chip. Bait the Q chain, Soul Unbound out through the knockups, and punish the 14s Q window while you stack anti-heal.

edits.before: By level 3 it evens out into a skill matchup — if you can weave your Q dashes and E to dodge his center Q hits, you trade fine, but he re-tilts it at 4-5 and especially 6 when World Ender comes online. His R all-in with the healing, stat boost, and takedown fear is far scarier than your ultimate at this stage, so avoid extended fights while it's up and play for the wave.
edits.after: Level 3 does not even it out: Umbral Dash (9s at rank 1) heals him back through your Q pokes, and the centre of Infernal Chains grounds you — inside it your Q3 dash and Fate Sealed do not fire, so leave it before you commit. At 6 World Ender's stats, healing and takedown extension beat your ultimate, so buy Executioner's Calling early and play the wave, not the duel.

edits.before: After your first item you start to pull ahead: your mixed AD/AP DPS, W shield, and E repositioning let you kite his Q chain and punish its long cooldown. With two-plus items you clearly out-scale — bait his Q, E through the knockups, and your sustained damage beats his single-target drain in a long fight.
edits.after: First item alone does not flip it — his healing still carries extended trades until Executioner's Calling lands. With two-plus items you clearly out-scale: mixed damage, Spirit Cleave's shield and Soul Unbound repositioning let you bait the Q chain, ride out the knockups, and win the long fight.
